sense: at some time in the future

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.4: huic utinam aliquandō grātiam referre possīmus! (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Mil. 69: illūcēscet aliquandō ille diēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: An indefinite time, past, present or future; in a negative or doubtful clause “ever” is umquam.

evidence: Verg. A. 1.203: forsan et haec ōlim meminisse juvābit
terms.comment: Usually “once, long ago” (see once upon a time); of the future, Lewis & Short call it rare but classical.

phrases.latin: forsan et haec ōlim meminisse juvābit
phrases.english: perhaps one day it will be a joy to remember even this

sources: Lewis & Short: aliquando · Lewis & Short: olim
